correctness.rationale: PASS: The feedback map x+=theta x and theta+=theta+c(1-theta)theta x is precisely the symmetric two-voter recurrence. u=1-theta decreases; telescoping x-x+=ux, u-u+=c theta(x-x+) produces strict eventually-necessary tests u>cx and u<c theta x for the two open basins. Order preservation and the exact growth ratio for two putative critical u sequences show uniqueness, since any critical sequence has n u_n->1. On a critical orbit w=u-cx increases to zero with increment c u²x; summing gives u=cx-(c²/2)x²+O(x³), hence 1/x_{n+1}-1/x_n=c+(c²/2)x_n+O(x_n²). With x_n=1/(cn)+O(log n/n²), summable increments yield a finite H in 1/x_n=cn+(c/2)log n+H+o(1). Boundary theta0=0 is one-step consensus; 0<c<=1,a<=1/2 make monotonicity strict; no multi-agent extrapolation.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge. Ohlin–Bencherki–Tegling establish the exact feedback and a sufficient consensus condition ca+theta0<1, noting it does not identify the full boundary; the full source does not provide a unique sharp critical threshold or logarithmic critical relaxation. Search of published findings returned the same submitted result, without stronger equivalent coverage; other concatenated FJ models prescribe different update laws. No general theorem in checked sources produces this coefficient c/2 for the feedback separatrix automatically.
residual_risks: Possible unindexed subsequent analysis of the exact symmetric voting map could already identify the critical separatrix or its correction.
Does not apply to asymmetric stubbornness, larger networks, or stochastic feedback; threshold has no closed elementary formula.
